intro.heading: TradingView is your workspace, not just a pretty chart.
intro.body: You are using it to read price, change perspective with timeframes, and mark behavior so your eyes stop feeling lost. A horizontal level marking a repeated reaction area is one of the cleanest beginner tools — you don't need every feature, just a few used clearly.
intro.dayliNote: You do not need every feature. A few tools used clearly is better than a messy chart.

tapCards.prompt: You want to mark a level price keeps reacting to. Which tool fits best?

options.label: A single horizontal level
options.feedback: Right — one clean level beats a cluttered chart every time.

options.label: Every drawing tool at once
options.feedback: Piling on tools usually makes the chart harder to read, not easier.

tapCards.prompt: Your chart now has 12 different lines, boxes, and indicators layered on top of price. What's the actual effect on your read?

options.label: It gets harder to see what price is actually doing
options.feedback: Exactly — clutter competes with price for your attention.

options.label: It gets easier — more markings means more information
options.feedback: More markings isn't automatically more useful information.

tapCards.prompt: You switch from the 4H to the 1M chart. What actually changed?

options.label: Your zoomed-in view of the same market — not the market itself
options.feedback: Right — timeframe changes your perspective, not the underlying price story.

options.label: You're now looking at a completely different market
options.feedback: It's still the same instrument and price — just a different zoom level.

quiz.question: A new trader adds ten different drawing tools to her chart at once, hoping more markings will make her read clearer. What's the better approach, and why?
options: A few tools used clearly — an overloaded chart makes price harder to read, not easier
More tools always means a better read
It doesn't matter how many tools she uses
quiz.explanation: A cluttered chart competes with price for your attention instead of clarifying it.

quiz.question: Does adding more drawing tools to a chart automatically make analysis more accurate?
options: No — a cluttered chart makes it harder to see what price is actually doing
Yes — more tools always means more accuracy
Only if the tools are different colors
quiz.explanation: A few clearly-used tools usually beat a chart covered in every available drawing tool.

quiz.question: Switching timeframes changes your ___ on the same market, not the market itself.
quiz.explanation: Zooming in or out just changes what detail you can see, not the underlying price story.
